title: Lemon Poppy Seed Scones
description: Make Chef John-level lemon poppy seed scones that are delightfully tender thanks to a slightly messy countertop method followed by a quick 2-ingredient strawberry glaze.
ingredients: 1 stick very cold unsalted butter, cut into cubes
1 tablespoon lemon zest, or more to taste
0.33333334326744 cup whole milk, or more as needed
1 cup powdered sugar, or more as needed

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).

Place self-rising flour in a large bowl. Cut in butter using a pastry blender until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Add poppy seeds, sugar, and lemon zest; mix to combine. Make a well in the center and pour in egg, lemon juice, and milk. Mix with a fork until dough starts to come together. Scoop up with one hand until a shaggy dough forms.

Pour dough out onto your work surface. Use your hands and a bench scraper to gather and press dough into a neat rectangle about 1- to 1-1/2-inches tall. Cut into 4 squares and then diagonally into 8 triangles. Space scones evenly onto a silicone-lined baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until bottoms are golden brown, about 25 minutes. Let cool in pan for 5 minutes, then transfer onto a wire rack to cool completely, about 30 minutes.

Mash strawberries finely to resemble a puree. Whisk in powdered sugar in batches to make a thick, spreadable glaze. Spread glaze over the cooled scones. Let scones cool on the rack until glaze hardens, about 20 minutes.

video.description: Make brunch or teatime extra special with these tender lemon poppy seed scones covered in fresh strawberry glaze. You'll create the signature shaggy dough by cutting cold butter into a mixture of self-rising flour enlivened with poppy seeds, lemon juice, and lemon zest. The method that follows is easy, though a little messy by necessity, as you'll gather and shape the dough on the counter rather than in the bowl, ensuring a tender texture. While they bake, you can whip up a simple 2-ingredient glaze by adding powdered sugar to mashed fresh strawberries. The hardest part is waiting for the scones to cool before glazing them! Get Chef John's recipe for [Lemon Poppy Seed Scones](https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/273654/lemon-poppy-seed-scones-with-fresh-strawberry-glaze/).
